source_text: Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων ἔφη· Ὑπὸ τῶν τοσούτων γραφῶν δυσωπούμενος οὐκ οἶδα τί φῶ περὶ τῆς γραφῆς ἣν ἔφη Ἡσαΐας, καθ᾿ ἣν ὁ θεὸς οὐδενὶ ἑτέρῳ δοῦναι τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ λέγει, οὕτως εἰπών· Ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ θεός, τοῦτό μου ὄνομα, τὴν δόξαν μου ἑτέρῳ οὐ μὴ δώσω οὐδὲ τὰς ἀρετάς μου . Κἀγώ· Εἰ μὲν ἁπλῶς καὶ μὴ μετὰ κακὶας τούτους τοὺς λόγους εἰπὼν ἐσίγησας, ὦ Τρύφων, μήτε τοὺς πρὸ αὐτῶν προειπὼν μήτε τοὺς ἐπακολουθοῦντας συνάψας, συγγνωστὸς εἶ, εἰ δὲ χάριν τοῦ νομίζειν δύνασθαι εἰς ἀπορίαν ἐμβάλλειν τὸν λόγον, ἵνα εἴπω ἐναντίας εἶναι τὰς γραφὰς ἀλλήλαις, πεπλάνησαι· οὐ γὰρ τολμήσω τοῦτό ποτε ἢ ἐνθυμηθῆναι ἢ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλ᾿ ἐὰν τοιαύτη τις δοκοῦσα εἶναι γραφὴ προβληθῇ, καὶ πρόφασιν ἔχῃ ὡς ἐναντία οὖσα, ἐκ παντὸς πεπεισμένος ὅτι οὐδεμία γραφὴ τῇ ἑτέρᾳ ἐναντία ἐστίν, αὐτὸς μὴ νοεῖν μᾶλλον ὁμολογήσω τὰ εἰρημένα, καὶ τοὺς ἐναντίας τὰς γραφὰς ὑπολαμβάνοντας τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν μᾶλλον ἐμοὶ πεῖσαι ἀγωνίσομαι. Ὅπως δ᾿ ἂν ᾖς προτεθεικὼς τὸ πρόβλημα, θεὸς ἐπίσταται. Ἐγὼ δὲ ὡς εἴρηται ὁ λόγος ἀναμνήσω ὑμᾶς, ὅπως καὶ ἐξ αὐτοῦ τούτου γνωρίσητε ὅτι ὁ θεὸς τῷ Χριστῷ αὐτοῦ μόνῳ τὴν δόξαν δίδωσιν. Ἀναλήψομαι δὲ βραχεῖς τινας λόγους, ὦ ἄνδρες, τοὺς ἐν συναφείᾳ τῶν εἰρημένων ὑπὸ τοῦ Τρύφωνος καὶ τοὺς ὁμοίως συνημμένους κατ᾿ ἐπακολούθησιν· οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἑτέρας περικοπῆς αὐτοὺς ἐρῶ, ἀλλ᾿ ὑφ᾿ ἓν ὥς εἰσι συνημμένοι· καὶ ὑμεῖς τὸν νοῦν χρήσατέ μοι. Εἰσὶ δὲ οὗτοι· Οὕτως λέγει κύριος ὁ θεός, ὁ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ πήξας αὐτόν, ὁ στερεώσας τὴν γῆν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ διδοὺς πνοὴν τῷ λαῷ τῷ ἐπ᾿ αὐτῆς καὶ πνεῦμα τοῖς πατοῦσιν αὐτήν. Ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἐκάλεσά σε ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, καὶ κρατήσω τῆς χειρός σου καὶ ἰσχύσω σε, καὶ ἔδωκά σε εἰς διαθήκην γένους, εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν, ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς τυφλῶν, ἐξαγαγεῖν ἐκ δεσμῶν πεπεδημένους καὶ ἐξ οἴκου φυλακῆς καθημένους ἐν σκότει. Ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ θεός, τοῦτό μου ὄνομα, τὴν δόξαν μου ἑτέρῳ οὐ μὴ δώσω οὐδὲ τὰς ἀρετάς μου τοῖς γλυπτοῖς. Τὰ ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς ἰδοὺ ἥκει, καινὰ ἃ ἐγὼ ἀναγγέλλω. καὶ πρὸ τοῦ ἀναγγεῖλαι ἐδηλώθη ὑμῖν. Ὑμνήσατε τῷ θεῷ ὕμνον καινόν· ἀρχὴ αὐτοῦ ἀπ᾿ ἄκρου τῆς γῆς· οἱ καταβαίνοντες τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πλέοντες, αἱ νῆσοι καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες αὐτάς. Εὐφράνθητι ἔρημος καὶ αἱ κῶμαι αὐτῶν καὶ αἱ ἐπαύλεις, καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες Κηδάρ εὐφρανθήσονται, καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες πέτραν ἀπ᾿ ἄκρου τῶν ὀρέων βοήσονται, δώσουσι τῷ θεῷ δόξαν, τὰς ἀρετάς αὐτοῦ ἐν ταῖς νήσοις ἀναγγελοῦσι. Κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῶν δυνάμεων ἐξελεύσεται, συντρίψει πόλεμον, ἐπεγερεῖ ζῆλον καὶ βοήσεται ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐχθροὺς μετ᾿ ἰσχύος . Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἔφην πρὸς αὐτούς· Νενοήκατε, ὧ φίλοι, ὅτι ὁ θεὸς λέγει δώσειν τούτῳ, ὃν εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν κατέστησε, δόξαν καὶ οὐκ ἄλλῳ τινί, ἀλλ᾿ οὐχ, ὡς ἔφη Τρύφων, ὡς ἑαυτῷ κατέχοντος τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δόξαν; Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων ἀπεκρίνατο· Νενοήκαμεν καὶ τοῦτο· πέραινε τοιγαροῦν καὶ τὰ ἐπίλοιπα τοῦ λόγου.
pass_a_gloss: And Trypho said, Being distressed by so many writings, I do not know what to say concerning the writing which Isaiah said, according to which God says He will not give His glory to another, having spoken thus: I am the Lord God, this is My name, I will not give My glory to another, nor My virtues. And I said, If you have spoken these words simply and not with malice, having been silent and not having spoken the preceding words nor having connected the following words, you are excusable, but if for the sake of seeming to be able to cast the word into doubt, so that I might say the writings are contrary to each other, you have been deceived; for I will not dare to think or say this, but if some writing seems to be such and has a pretext as being contrary, being convinced that no writing is contrary to another, I will confess that I do not understand what has been said, and I will strive to persuade those who think the writings are contrary to think the same as me. But how you have proposed the problem, God knows. And I will remind you of the word as has been said, so that you may also know from this that God gives His glory to His Christ alone. I will take up a few words, men, which are connected with what has been said by Trypho and which are similarly connected in sequence; for I will not speak them from another passage, but as they are connected under one heading; and you use your mind for me. These words are: Thus says the Lord God, who made the heaven and established it, who strengthened the earth and what is in it, and gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who tread on it. I, the Lord God, have called you in righteousness, and I will hold your hand and strengthen you, and I have given you as a covenant to the nation, as a light to the nations, to open the eyes of the blind, to bring out those who are bound from prison and those who sit in darkness in the house of guard. I, the Lord God, this is My name, I will not give My glory to another, nor My virtues to the carved images. The things from the beginning, behold, have come, new things which I announce; and before I announce them, they have been revealed to you. Sing a new hymn to God; the beginning of it is from the end of the earth; those who go down to the sea and sail, the islands and those who inhabit them. Let the desert and its villages and pastures rejoice, and those who inhabit Kedar will rejoice, and those who inhabit the rock from the end of the mountains will shout, they will give glory to God, they will announce His virtues in the islands. The Lord God of hosts will go out, He will crush war, He will arouse zeal and shout upon the enemies with strength. And having said these things, I said to them: Have you perceived, friends, that God says He will give glory to this one, whom He has established as a light to the nations, and not to another, but not, as Trypho said, as if God holds His glory for Himself? And Trypho responded: We have perceived this too; proceed therefore with the rest of the word.

pass_b_english: Trypho said, "Overwhelmed by so many passages, I do not know what to say about the passage Isaiah spoke, in which God declares He will not give His glory to another, putting it like this: 'I am the Lord God; this is My name. I will not give My glory to another, nor My virtues' (Isaiah 42:8)." I replied, "If you have spoken these words simply and without malice — having kept silent about what precedes them and without connecting what follows — you are excusable. But if you do it to make it seem you can throw the argument into confusion so that I would say the Scriptures contradict each other, you are deceived. I will never dare to think or say such a thing. Rather, if some passage appears to have a pretext of being contrary, since I am convinced that no Scripture contradicts another, I will admit that I do not understand what has been said, and I will strive to persuade those who think the Scriptures contradict each other to think as I do. How you have framed the problem, God knows. As has been said, I will remind you of the passage so that you may also know from it that God gives His glory to His Christ alone. I will take up a few brief words, men, that are connected with what Trypho said and that follow in the same sequence; for I will not cite them from another section, but as they are joined together under one heading. So attend with your minds. They are these: 'Thus says the Lord God, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and what comes from it, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk on it' (Isaiah 42:5). 'I, the Lord God, have called you in righteousness; I will take hold of your hand and keep you; I have given you as a covenant for the people, a light for the nations, to open eyes that are blind, to bring out prisoners from the dungeon and those who sit in darkness from the prison house' (Isaiah 42:6-7). 'I am the Lord God; that is My name. I will not give My glory to another, nor My virtues to carved idols' (Isaiah 42:8). 'See, the former things have come to pass, and new things I declare; before they spring up I tell you of them' (Isaiah 42:9). 'Sing to the Lord a new song, His praise from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea and all that is in it, you islands and all who live in them' (Isaiah 42:10). 'Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices; let the settlements where Kedar lives rejoice. Let the people of Sela sing for joy; let them shout from the mountaintops. Let them give glory to the Lord and proclaim His praise in the islands' (Isaiah 42:11-12). 'The Lord will march out like a champion, like a warrior He will stir up His zeal; with a shout He will raise the battle cry and will triumph over His enemies' (Isaiah 42:13)." Having said these things, I said to them, "Have you perceived, friends, that God says He will give glory to this One, whom He has appointed as a light to the nations, and not to another? Not, as Trypho said, as though God were keeping His glory for Himself?" And Trypho answered, "We have perceived this too; proceed then with the rest of the argument."

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the dialogue and the lengthy series of Isaiah quotations. Pass B provides necessary scripture citations (Isaiah 42:5-13) which correspond to the Greek text provided. Pass A is a faithful literal rendering. The distinction between Trypho's misunderstanding and Justin's argument regarding God's glory is preserved.
